about.text: Pendidam is a traditional skimmed fermented milk of Cameroon's Far North, sold in periodic markets. Raw milk is filtered and heated to about 60 to 70 °C, inoculated and left at 28 to 35 °C for one to three days to curdle, then churned into a whisked curd; the butter is skimmed off in a calabash, leaving the fermented skimmed milk.
